mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a tightening labor market, which historically correlates with wage inflation and subsequent monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases below 3.5% and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate activity (HOUST) signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of increasing HOUST (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a weakening supply side, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and subsequent negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 2%, and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, the combined signal indicates aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, the combined signal indicates strong consumer demand and labor market tightness, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: strong demand and tight labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of RSAFS and UNRATE on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs per month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and subsequent positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeding 3% quarter-over-quarter, and industrial production (INDPRO) increasing by more than 0.5% month-over-month, the combined signal indicates robust economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 3% QoQ and INDPRO increases > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of GDPC1 and INDPRO on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
